'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Operation Barkhane]]
***[[France]] formally ends its [[Interventionism (politics)|military intervention]] in [[Mali]] after withdrawing its last remaining troops from a military base in [[Gao]]. The base was handed over to [[Malian Armed Forces]] before the French forces crossed into neighbouring [[Niger]]. [https://www.ecofinagency.com/public-management/1608-43790-france-withdraws-the-last-barkhane-unit-from-mali (Ecofin Agency)]
**Four [[Russia]]n [[Wagner Group]] [[paramilitaries]] are killed during an ambush by [[Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin]] militants in [[Bandiagara]]. [https://www.africanews.com/2022/08/16/mali-jihadist-group-claims-to-have-killed-four-russian-wagner-group-mercenaries/ (Africanews)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Fall of Kabul (2021)|Fall of Kabul]]
***The [[Taliban]] stages a Victory Day parade on the first anniversary of the [[Fall of Kabul (2021)|capture]] of [[Kabul]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/pictures/afghanistan-taliban-victory-day-us-withdrawal/ (CBS News)]
*[[Israeli–Syrian ceasefire line incidents during the Syrian civil war]]
**[[Israel]] launches a series of [[airstrike]]s on [[Damascus]] and [[Tartus]], [[Syria]], killing three [[Syrian Army|soldiers]] and injuring three others. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/8/14/israeli-air-strikes-in-syria-kills-three-soldiers-state-media (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] approves a [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] aimed at targeting the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant|Omicron variant]] and other [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|variants]] of [[SARS-CoV-2]], becoming the first country to do so. [https://euroweeklynews.com/2022/08/15/uk-approves-use-of-next-generation-covid-vaccine-that-targets-original-strain-and-omicron-variants/ (''EuroWeekly News'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Liberia–United States relations]]
**The United States imposes [[Economic sanctions|sanctions]] on three senior members of the [[Cabinet of Liberia|cabinet]] of [[President of Liberia|Liberian president]] [[George Weah]], accusing them of corruption. [https://apnews.com/article/george-weah-government-and-politics-c602d2dab6b91daaada07ea58db67437 (AP)]
*[[New Zealand Prime Minister|Prime minister of New Zealand]] [[Jacinda Ardern]] announces the deployment of 120 [[New Zealand troops]] to the United Kingdom to train [[Ukrainian forces]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/nz-deploy-120-troops-britain-train-ukrainian-troops-2022-08-15/ (Reuters)] 

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**The [[State Administration Council|military junta]] court sentences former [[State Counsellor of Myanmar|state counsellor]] [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] to six years in prison for [[Corruption in Myanmar|corruption]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20220815-myanmar-junta-court-jails-suu-kyi-for-six-years-for-corruption (France 24)]
*A lawsuit is filed against the [[Central Intelligence Agency]] and its former [[Director of the Central Intelligence Agency|director]] [[Mike Pompeo]], accusing the agency of spying on lawyers and journalists who met with [[Julian Assange]]. [https://www.axios.com/2022/08/15/cia-lawsuit-journalists-lawyers-assange-visit (''Axios'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2022 Kenyan general election]]
**The [[Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission]] declares [[William Ruto]] as the winner of the election. [https://apnews.com/article/africa-elections-presidential-kenya-41cec0a771a1fe7f0f5a0e83761b03a9 (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[FIFA]] suspends the [[All India Football Federation]] for violating its statutes on third-party interference. India is stripped of its hosting rights for [[international football]] tournaments, including the [[2022 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup]] scheduled for October 2022. [https://www.dw.com/en/fifa-suspends-all-india-football-federation/a-62816839 (Deutsche Welle)]
